Subject: POC plan & success criteria — recap from today's call

Hi Tom / Aisha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap so we have shared expectations and next steps for the POC:

Scope (what we'll evaluate):
- Use case A: real-time customer support summarization (API integration w/ 1,200 daily conversations)
- Use case B: customer intent classification for routing into teams (batch inference on daily digest)

Success criteria (initial):
- Summarization: average ROUGE-L >= 0.48 on the sample set + human QA accept rate >= 85%
- Classification: accuracy >= 92% on the annotated dataset
- Latency: median token latency < 90ms for interactive flows on Dedicated dev pool

Timeline & ownership:
- Kickoff + data handoff: Jan 27 (you provide sample conversations and labels)
- Setup & baseline run: Jan 28–Feb 3 (Dev + Rishi)
- Evaluation & review: Feb 4–10 (Marissa / Evelyn / FinTech reviewers)

Attachments: POC_Scope_v1.pdf (detailed tasks, data requirements, and basic test plan).

Next steps:
1) Tom — confirm you can share the redacted conversation samples and label set by Jan 27.
2) We'll schedule a 30-min kickoff next week to confirm access and scope.
3) If anything else needs to be added to scope, flag it now so we can re-baseline before the setup window.

Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Regards,
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple of things from our side after syncing with ops:
1) We want to add a third use case mid-trial: Use case C — transaction anomaly detection (near real-time scoring for flags). Priority: medium.
2) For summarization success criteria, can we move the threshold to ROUGE-L >= 0.45 if the human QA accept rate is >= 88%? Our reviewers value precision of highlights over recall.
3) We'll share a redacted dataset for A+B by Jan 27; for C we'll need an additional schema and ~2k labeled examples — can deliver by Feb 5.

If adding C means a longer setup window or additional engineering effort, let us know and we'll accommodate (we have some flexibility on the overall end date).

Tom

Marissa / team —

Quick technical assessment after reviewing the sample schemas and Tom's note:
- Adding Use Case C (anomaly detection) is feasible but requires:
  1) an ingestion adapter for transaction events (2–3 days)
  2) a feature extraction pipeline + labeling validator (3–4 days)
  3) an eval harness for streaming scoring and false-positive analysis (2 days)

Estimate (engineering effort): 7–9 full dev days (split across 2 engineers).
Impact to timeline: we should shift the setup & baseline window by one week to give FinTech time to deliver the labeled C dataset (they said Feb 5). Proposed new window: Feb 4–Feb 12.

Ownership suggestions:
- Dev Patel: ingestion & feature pipeline (owner)
- Rishi Malhotra: model tuning + latency testing
- Evelyn Hart: acceptance tests and coordinating FinTech reviewer sessions

Attachments: initial_eval_results.csv (baseline metrics for A+B), and I drafted an updated scope (POC_Scope_v2-rebaseline.pdf).

Open question for Sales: does adding C change pricing or do we absorb within the POC? I'd recommend a small scope addendum (proposal email to procurement) to set expectations; Laura, can you advise on whether we need a formal sign-off?

—Dev
